newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania average one-week rate soars to 125.45 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania average one-week rate soars to 125.45 pct.

text.p: The average rate on Romania's central bank's one-week funds soared to 125.45 percent at Thursday's refinancing auction, the highest since mid-1994, from 90 percent last week, central bank (BNR) data showed.
The BNR's one-week funds offer of 600 billion lei was heavily oversubscribed, with six banks entering bids worth a total 1.76 trillion lei, at rates ranging from 90 percent to 151 percent.

The rate hike is expected to trigger a jump of the Lombard rate, which now is set by multiplying the average one-week auctioned rate by 1.6. The Lombard rate, applied to overdraft credits, was previously set at 90 percent.

Interbank traders said short-term rates, which closed Thursday hovering near 93 percent, were expected to rise following the upswing in the BNR's key rates as the money market was facing leu shortages.
Over the past two months the BNR has started to tighten monetary policy, in order to control a surge in inflation.

Year-on-year inflation, which rose to 56.9 percent last year against a 20 percent target, is forecast to rise to 97 percent in 1997, after January's fuel price rise, and planned electricity and food price libearlisation.
